member.name: T:Physics.Wasm.PhysicsBridge
member.summary:
The entire JS-facing surface of the physics simulation. Mirrors 's own "opaque handles + primitives only" design one level further out: every handle here is a plain int id minted by this class (never a raw Bepu or Physics handle value), and every shape/pose parameter is individual doubles rather than a struct, because that's what the built-in JSExport marshaler understands without any custom interop glue. Variable-length data (point clouds, triangle soups) crosses as a flat double[] [x0,y0,z0,x1,y1,z1,...] marked with , and every multi-value result comes back as a flat double[] whose layout is documented on the method.
The whole API is exposed here - there is deliberately nothing left that only the desktop (Godot) build can call. TypeScript mirrors this surface 1:1 in PhysicsBridgeContract.ts, and everything above it (command batching, entity ids, character carry, snapshots) lives in TypeScript - this file stays a thin marshalling layer.
Intended caller: PhysicsWorker.ts, once per fixed-timestep tick: const packed = PhysicsBridge.Step(dt); // Float64 stride StepStride (14) per body const events = PhysicsBridge.GetLastOverlapEvents(); // Int32 stride 3 per event

member.name: M:Physics.Wasm.PhysicsBridge.AddConvexHullShape(System.Double[],System.Double)
member.summary: Builds a convex hull from a flat point cloud [x0,y0,z0,x1,...]. Returns [shapeId, centroidOffsetX, centroidOffsetY, centroidOffsetZ]: Bepu re-centres the hull on its own centroid, and the offset (in the input points' local space) must be added - rotated by the body's orientation - to the source origin when building the pose, or the hull appears shifted. PhysicsWorld.ts does that for you.

member.name: M:Physics.Wasm.PhysicsBridge.Step(System.Double)
member.summary: Advances the simulation and returns every dynamic/kinematic body's fresh state as a flat buffer: [bodyId, posX, posY, posZ, quatX, quatY, quatZ, quatW, linVelX, linVelY, linVelZ, angVelX, angVelY, angVelZ] ( doubles) repeated once per body currently registered, in unspecified order. Call GetLastOverlapEvents() immediately after to read this same step's Entered/Exited transitions.

member.name: M:Physics.Wasm.PhysicsBridge.GetLastOverlapEvents
member.summary: Flat buffer from the most recent Step(): [ownerIdA, ownerIdB, entered(0/1)] per event.
